title: Measurement of Space Charge Layers using Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Grain boundaries play an important role in determining the properties of many functional ceramics [1-2]. In particular, in ionic conductors, grain boundaries can act as pathways or roadblocks to the flow of charge. Such effects are mediated by space charges, which are regions of non-uniform charge that develop in response to defect redistributions towards internal interfaces in ionic solids. Characterizing the electrical potential build-up at such space charge regions (the space charge potential) and the extent of this build-up (the space charge width) is critical. In particular, the couplings between grain boundary structure, chemistry, and space charge potential are poorly understood, both due to the difficulty in characterizing these properties and the complexity and diversity of grain boundary structures.
